title: Reduce syscalls for inode configuration
description:
Strategies to employ
`open` with `O_CREAT|O_EXCL` in order to optimize for the more common scenario where the file does not already exist; thus we can know the mode, owner and group of the file in a single call; Do the full compliment of syscalls only on `EEXIST`.
 * Set mode from zip headers (make our umask open first)
 * Adjust owner only if differs from our euid/egid (at least unless/until we want to concern ourselves with overriding setgid directory behavior, which could cause our assumption about the new inode's group to be wrong)

Keep file handles from our `open` calls around until all parts including that file have completed. This has two benefits:
1. Avoids an issue when running rootless where we set the mode to readonly on the open call, which prevents a subsequent open for writing from succeeding
2. Slightly reduced open/close call count

Put a thread-local cache of directory handles (maybe even just one) and use it with `openat` on nth files to avoid repeated full tree walks.

title: Improved support for rootless and btrfsless operation
description:
Goals:
1. Make the expected behavior with regards to ownership preservation explicit as CLI arg, error if unable to fulfill
2. Make the expected behavior with regards to encoded writes explicit as CLI arg, error if unable to fulfill (because not root or because destination is not BTRFS).
  a) `--write-mode auto|compressed|decompressed`, this format allows future options such as hybrid based on page cache writeback
3. Don't try encoded writes literally a million times and fall back to decompressed each time, just base it on the upfront configured write mode

title: Implement object upload
description:
The current burst-writer can only write to disk.

We should keep this binary because:
* Various integration tests use it, e.g. to verify the results are valid according to 7zz or zipinfo
* The core writer logic does not require the megabytes of additional AWS dependencies to interface with S3, so there may be some applications for a compact and easy to build static writer.

So instead, let's pull out any logic currently unique to the writer into a library and then make the burst-writer binary link statically to it. Then, let's refactor the burst-downloader argument parsing so that it accepts subcommands `put` and `restore`.

`put` will use the burst-writer library to generate a BURST archive stream, but then directly upload it to S3 using multipart uploads. Chunk size should be configurable in multiples of 8 MiB from a command line flag, as when downloading.

`restore` will work as the downloader works today.

title: Sniff for BRST EOCD comment, fall back to boring sequential download if absent
description:
In case users point the downloader at ZIP objects that were not generated by the BURST writer, we should begin a framework to successfully, if slowly and boringly, process them.

Eventually it would be nice for this to directly support zip files by fetching the full CD and then sequentially extracting it, as well as various compressed tarballs by simply shelling out to `tar` with appropriate arguments, if it's available.

File type could be detected by S3 content type response header or in the case of zips, by the EOCD magic as well.

The value proposition for this work is that it would allow users to write archives to S3 in the most convenient format at the time for the system/environment generating the archive, and allow sites with substantial existing data in S3 archives to easily migrate to BURST by switching to the BURST downloader and progressively rewriting their S3 objects.

title: Formalize central directory ordering requirement
description:
The partial CD processing optimization requires that the CD entries be in the same order they occur in the physical archive.

The writer happens to do this currently but it is not a documented requirement of the format and there is no test coverage to ensure this remains true in future.

The zip standard in general allows CD entries to be in any order, so this is a BURST specialization.
